source: make_psr2.py in the Gen 2 derivation folder, from the psr sweep logs; do not edit by hand
core: pokemon-speedrunning/gambatte-core 5a41a68c25402421fb1983ddadc9faf2418ddb0f built with g++ 13.3.0 -O2 -std=c++14 -DREVISION=0 -DHAVE_CSTDINT; harness gen2tid.cpp in the derivation folder
frame_convention: all frame numbers are 0-based harness frame indices from power-on (frame 0 = the first frame after power-on; on GBP including gambatte's GBA->CGB stall); one frame = 70224 cycles = 35112 audio samples; seconds = frames / (4194304/70224)
what_this_is: A multi-step 'prescribed sequence' methodology, added BESIDE the single-tap hold-start-v1 and not replacing it. The approach is the Gen 2 speedrunning community's; what is here is a derived table for it. Instead of one timed tap on NEW GAME, the script backs out of the main menu a fixed number of times, waits a measured number of frames, optionally steps through OPTION, backs out again, then presses A on NEW GAME and HOLDS IT until the game rolls. Holding the press out removes the tap-length question entirely.
buffering: Every press except the START that reaches the menu and the timed wait is BUFFERED: the harness holds the button from the moment the step begins and the game accepts it on the first frame it can (B is held up to 16 frames for a backout; START is held until the menu reloads; the NEW GAME A is held until the roll). A human reproduces this by holding the button through the transition rather than tapping it. A press that is tapped LATE rather than buffered shifts every later frame and changes the result: this is the single most likely way to miss.
timed_elements: the START that reaches the main menu, anywhere inside its hold plateau - wide, and absent entirely on routes whose plateau begins at power-on
each backout: the switch from B to START, about 16 frames after the menu and anywhere from 10 to 64 - but NOT once the title screen has finished appearing, which is past the deadline
the OPTION step, if the route has one: A goes down 8 frames after DOWN, with a 4-frame window
the wait, which must land inside its 4-frame poll bin (67 ms)
timed_elements_note: An earlier version of this data claimed only two things were timed. That was wrong: a backout and the OPTION step each carry their own deadline, and a person told otherwise would miss them.

credits.what: Multi-step prescribed input sequences - buffered backouts, a measured wait, and a NEW GAME press held out rather than tapped - are the community's, worked out over years of research and published in their route documents, script pastebins and bruteforcers. This tool did not invent that approach and does not claim to. What is ours is a sweep and a table for one game on one console, built on top of it.

Reviewed the helper and pointed out that its Gen 2 method did not reflect how these manipulations are actually performed - that there are prescribed sequences for each one, that community New Game A presses are buffered and so held out longer, and that holding the press out beats a 4-8 frame tap - and said to start from the existing community research. Thank you: that feedback is why this was derived, and the shape of it follows what they described.
gambatte-core, the cycle-accurate core every one of the 288,144 boots in this sweep ran on.
pokecrystal, which establishes where and when wPlayerID is written on the New Game path.

credits.who: the authors of the published Gold and Silver TID scripts
credits.what: The community script TIDs (pastebins ZF4QX7Ya and HEXruHKq) are what the original single-press tables were checked against. This methodology's no-backout case reproduces those tables bin for bin, so their work is what the derivation below ultimately rests on.

credit_note: These credits name the people and projects whose work this methodology rests on or came from. The approach is the community's; the contribution here is a derived table for Crystal on a Game Boy Player. None of them endorse this tool, have checked it, or agree with what it says.

gbp.name: prescribed sequence: hold START to the menu, buffered backouts, a measured wait, then A held out on NEW GAME
gbp.console_name: GBA silicon booted with the CGB boot ROM and the GBA flag: GameCube Game Boy Player, GBA / GBA SP
gbp.predicts: the Trainer ID, the Lucky ID and the Secret ID
gbp.status: emulator-derived on gambatte-core; NOT confirmed on hardware and NOT executed by any human. Its degenerate case reproduces the shipped crystal/gbp/hold-start-v1 table on all 599 overlapping bins (asserted at build time), which is evidence the harness is right, not that a person can perform it.
gbp.validation: STRUCTURAL: the script steps are the harness's own (gen2tid.cpp "psr"). EMPIRICAL: 576144 boots. CROSS-CHECK against the shipped single-press table over 599 overlapping bins: 599 identical, 0 differ.
steps: Clear the save (Up+B+Select on the title) so the menu shows NEW GAME with no CONTINUE, then POWER THE CONSOLE OFF. Every frame number below is counted from power-on, so the run has to start from one.
Hold START from power-on until the main menu appears - or, for a route whose plateau does not start at 0, press START inside the frame window the route names.

Back out and return to the menu 'pre' times: press B, then about 16 frames later (a quarter second) press START and hold it until the menu comes back. Do NOT wait for the title screen to finish appearing - that is already too late.
Wait the stated number of frames. The route counts from the menu DETECTOR, which is 4 frames before the box is drawn, so the printed count from the visible box is 4 lower.
If the route says OPTION: press DOWN, then press A 8 frames later, then hold START until the main menu reloads.
Back out and return 'post' more times, the same way.
Press A on NEW GAME and HOLD it. Do not release until the game has rolled.

step_frames.note: backout 109 is constant across all 16 plateaus and all 36,009 routes each; option 94 over 288,000 rows. About 0.06% of post-backouts run long (125/133/137) and a handful of NEW GAME presses land at +5 or +9 instead of +1 - those steps are buffered, so the storyboard is a frame or two out for them and nothing else is affected.

gbp.wait_anchor: W is counted from the menu DETECTOR (wMenuDataPointer == MainMenu.MenuData). The box is drawn visible_menu_lag_frames = 4 frames later, so a person anchoring on the box they can see must wait W - 4 frames, not W.

coverage.note: 20 Trainer IDs (0.03%) are not produced by any swept script; the helper falls back to the timed tap or says it has nothing.

gbp.route_ranking: widest hold plateau first, then fewest extra actions, then the shortest wait
gbp.code_layout: script_code_b64 is 3 bytes per Trainer ID, big-endian, holding a 20-bit value: plateau_index<<16 | pre<<14 | opt<<13 | post<<11 | (W/4). Only meaningful where covered_bitmap_b64 has the bit set.
gbp.alt_note: Alternate routes for the SAME Trainer ID with a DIFFERENT Lucky ID, so a specific (Trainer ID, Lucky ID) pair can be asked for rather than only a Trainer ID. One byte of count per Trainer ID, then a stream of 5-byte (LID, script code) records in the same easiest-first order. The primary route is NOT repeated here - it is in script_code_b64 and lid_b64. At most 4 alternates are kept per Trainer ID (the easiest ones): the sweep reaches more, but shipping all of them would cost about 2.5 MB in an offline bundle that is already the binding constraint.

gbp.rtc_tables_note: Extra tables for other cartridge-clock states, keyed by state. The top-level table is the days0 (fresh clock) state. A runner who resets repeatedly is only ever in days0 or days512 (the day-carry bit), because FixDays writes the day counter back mod 140 - every other bracket is a single-boot transient. Same packed layout as the primary table.
gbp.rtc_note: Gold and Silver select a table by the cartridge clock's day bracket. This sweep is the days0 bracket - the fresh-clock state a runner is in after the first boot, and what the community bruteforcer and GSE use. The other state a repeatedly-resetting runner can be in is days512 (the day-carry bit); it is NOT swept here.
gbp.status: emulator-derived on gambatte-core; NOT confirmed on hardware and NOT executed by any human. Its degenerate case reproduces the shipped gold/gbp/hold-start-v1 table on all 307 overlapping bins (asserted at build time), which is evidence the harness is right, not that a person can perform it.
gbp.validation: STRUCTURAL: the script steps are the harness's own (gen2tid.cpp "psr"). EMPIRICAL: 288072 boots. CROSS-CHECK against the shipped single-press table over 599 overlapping bins: 307 identical, 292 differ. The differences are expected and are not errors: the single-press derivation TAPS the NEW GAME press for 8 frames and releases it, while this method HOLDS it out until the roll. Measured, that shifts the Gen 2 RNG by exactly one step in Gold and Silver - every disagreement is +/-1 in one or both bytes. Crystal is unaffected and matches exactly. So this table is validated only in the weaker sense that its disagreements are all one step wide; no community-checked table exists for the held-out press in these two games.

not_derived: Any console other than the Game Boy Player: not swept. Hold plateaus and menu frames differ per platform, so these routes do not transfer.
GAMES ABSENT ALTOGETHER: only the games listed under "games" above have a table. Any Gen 2 game not listed there was not swept at all.
For whichever of Gold and Silver DO appear above: only the days0 RTC bracket (the fresh-clock state) is swept. The days512 day-carry state is not.

All the other Gold/Silver RTC brackets (140-511 days and the halted family): these are single-boot transients for a runner who resets repeatedly, so they are deliberately out of scope rather than merely undone.
Hardware: nothing here has been run on a real console, by anyone.
Human execution: no person has performed one of these scripts and reported the Trainer ID they got.
Plateaus beyond those swept, and waits beyond each table's wait_max_frames: not explored, so the uncovered Trainer IDs may well be reachable by a wider sweep.
